content.comment_body: Hello [user_name], first of all, thank you for sharing your success—it’s truly impressive. I appreciate learning about this challenge. I have a question: how can I manage the input and output of a [product_name] controller using Visual Studio? Thanks for everything.

Hello [user_name], if you have questions about controlling I/O of your [product_name] controller through iOS or Android, I can guide you step-by-step. For more details, search for my YouTube channel by typing [user_name], where you’ll find multiple videos. For your needs, try searching 'Controlling and Monitoring Your PLC inputs and outputs Through Your Android Smartphones' on Google or YouTube. Thanks in advance, [user_name].
Hello, I would like to know how to control the inputs on a PLC. I always thought inputs could only be read, not written to. Regards.

Hi [user_name], inputs of a PLC are read-only and cannot be written to. For example, it's not possible to activate an input opto-coupler without applying an external voltage to it. Hope this clarifies things.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are seeking ways to manage the I/O of [product_name] controllers using Visual Studio and mobile devices. There is some confusion around whether PLC inputs can be programmatically set—one user explains that inputs are inherently read-only and cannot be controlled directly by software. Overall, participants are interested in clearer guidance regarding the technical limitations and integration possibilities between [product_name] controllers and third-party platforms like Visual Studio and mobile operating systems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to control both inputs and outputs of their [product_name] controller through Visual Studio and potentially mobile applications, and are looking for solutions or guidance on how to achieve this.
